page: Amazon Web Services x8g.metal-48xl is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server configuration based on the 64-bit ARM architecture. The host is powered by AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processors operating at 2.7 GHz across 192 physical cores and 192 virtual CPUs with dedicated single-threaded execution per core. Hardware cache allocations comprise 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and 36 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 3072 GB of DDR5 RAM, yielding a high memory density of 16 GB per physical core. The system contains no bundled local NVMe storage and includes no discrete graphics processing units. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline throughput of 50 Gbps.

Performance benchmark results show exceptional parallel computing and memory performance. The server achieves top-tier results in stress-ng multi-core CPU testing and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression, alongside leading marks in software compilation and PassMark database operations. Memory subsystem tests report top-tier throughput, sustaining uncached large-block read bandwidth of 860.6 GB/sec and uncached write bandwidth of 409.74 GB/sec. In-memory data store testing demonstrates top-tier Redis SET operations surpassing 350 million operations per second, complemented by 148.87 GB/sec static web serving throughput. Single-core results in Geekbench and stress-ng remain within average mid-tier ranges, and language model text generation performance is constrained.

Qualitatively, the x8g.metal-48xl delivers substantial resource consolidation by packing 192 physical cores and three terabytes of DDR5 RAM into a single bare-metal host without virtualization overhead. The primary engineering tradeoff is the complete absence of integrated local storage, which requires all disk I/O to traverse network interfaces to attached block storage. As a result, the instance is targeted at large-scale, memory-bound workloads, including distributed in-memory databases, key-value stores, large-footprint enterprise caching tiers, large multi-threaded Clang compilation jobs, and high-concurrency data analytics.
description: Amazon Web Services x8g.metal-48xl is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server powered by 192 physical AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 cores based on the arm64 architecture, operating at 2.7 GHz with one thread per core. The configuration includes 3072 GB of DDR5 system memory, providing 16 GB of RAM per core, and delivers a baseline network throughput of 50 Gbps. It contains no onboard local storage, necessitating reliance on network-attached volumes, and features no dedicated GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluations show exceptional multi-core throughput, top-tier memory bandwidth exceeding 860 GB/s for large uncached reads, and strong database transaction execution, alongside top-tier Redis SET processing reaching 355 million operations per second. However, single-threaded processing remains average, and LLM text generation rates are limited. The instance offers significant resource density for memory-bound architectures, making it well matched for distributed in-memory caching systems, large enterprise databases, intensive software compilation pipelines, and massive multi-threaded parallel data processing.
